title: She Beat Myositis, Rebuilt Her Career, and Married the Man Behind The Family Man. Now Samantha Is Becoming a Mother.
excerpt: At 39, Samantha Ruth Prabhu is expecting her first child with filmmaker Raj Nidimoru — and she shot a chase scene while dealing with morning sickness to prove she's not slowing down.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Samantha Ruth Prabhu is expecting her first child at 39 with filmmaker Raj Nidimoru.
  • She confirmed her pregnancy during the success meet for her film *Maa Inti Bangaaram*.
  • Samantha filmed a chase scene while experiencing morning sickness, showcasing her dedication.
  • Her personal journey includes overcoming a public divorce and a myositis diagnosis.
  • With 37.9 million Instagram followers, she remains a significant figure in Indian cinema.
Samantha's Journey to Motherhood
›Due in December 2025 Expecting her first child with Raj Nidimoru.
›Film released on June 19, 2025 Confirmed pregnancy at *Maa Inti Bangaaram* success meet.
›Completed chase scene despite challenges Filmed while dealing with morning sickness.
›Diagnosed with myositis Overcame a public divorce and health struggles.
The photo dump landed on Instagram at midnight, and it told you everything you needed to know about where **Samantha Ruth Prabhu** is in her life right now. A candid shot in an ivory embroidered outfit, radiant and unhurried. Her two dogs curled up beside her on a bed. A gym video where she's working out with a visible baby bump, the kind of clip that makes you wonder how she still has that discipline. Breathtaking landscapes from a wellness retreat. A stack of books she's been reading. And tucked between the frames, quiet pictures with her husband, filmmaker **Raj Nidimoru** — the man who helped create *The Family Man* and, apparently, a very different kind of story with her. "June felt like a fairy tale," she captioned it. Coming from someone who spent the last four years navigating a public divorce, an autoimmune diagnosis, and a complete reinvention of her career, that sentence carries weight. https://www.instagram.com/p/DaS2yM8mn6Q/ ## The Announcement That Wasn't Really a Surprise Samantha confirmed her pregnancy at the success meet for **Maa Inti Bangaaram**, the Telugu film that has been quietly racking up numbers since its June 19 release. She showed up in a fitted white bodysuit and blue denim — no attempt to hide the bump, no coy deflection. The internet noticed. Two days later, she made it official. > "After Maa Inti Bangaaram, I will have to take a small break. Given my condition, I will have to take maternity leave. After that, I will be back with another film for my fans." — Samantha Ruth Prabhu > **"I'll see you when I see you." Classic Samantha — disarming, funny, and completely in control of her own narrative."** Then came the Instagram Story that broke the internet: a mirror selfie cradling her growing bump, captioned "My Six Pack. I'll see you when I see you." Classic Samantha — disarming, funny, and completely in control of her own narrative. According to reports, the baby is expected in December, almost exactly a year after Samantha and Raj tied the knot at the **Isha Foundation** on December 1, 2025. The wedding itself was intimate and private, a deliberate contrast to the years of tabloid noise that had followed her split from **Naga Chaitanya** in 2021. ## From Raji to Real Life ![Raj Nidimoru — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d7/Raj_%26_DK.jpg/3840px-Raj_%26_DK.jpg) Here's the thing about Samantha and Raj Nidimoru's love story that makes it feel like something out of a script they might actually write: she became a national sensation playing a Sri Lankan Tamil rebel in **The Family Man Season 2**, the show Raj co-created with **DK Krishna**. Her portrayal of Raji was so ferocious and layered that it single-handedly shifted her career from South Indian romantic lead to pan-Indian powerhouse. They reunited for **Citadel: Honey Bunny** on Prime Video, and somewhere between takes and table reads, life happened. What makes the pairing magnetic is the symmetry. He's the quiet architect behind some of India's sharpest long-form storytelling. She's the actress who walked through fire — a very public divorce, a **myositis diagnosis** that forced her to step away from work entirely — and came back looking stronger and more luminous than before. Together, they feel less like a celebrity couple and more like two people who found each other at exactly the right moment.

## She Shot a Chase Scene While Having Morning Sickness If you needed any more proof that Samantha doesn't do things halfway, here it is: she was already pregnant while filming *Maa Inti Bangaaram*. Director **Nandini Reddy** revealed that Samantha powered through a chase sequence while dealing with morning sickness. The crew initially thought she had a fever. The next day, Samantha casually told Nandini she was fine — just pregnant. "We took precautions to ensure she wasn't exhausted too much," Nandini said, which feels like the understatement of the year. The film itself has been a quiet commercial hit, proving once again that Samantha can open a movie on her name alone. For diaspora audiences, *Maa Inti Bangaaram* is expected to land on a major OTT platform after its theatrical window, though streaming details haven't been confirmed yet. ## What She Represents At 39, expecting her first child with a man she married after rebuilding her life from scratch, Samantha Ruth Prabhu has become something rare in Indian cinema — a star whose personal story is as compelling as anything she's done on screen. She didn't play it safe. She didn't disappear. She walked through every hard chapter publicly, with grace and occasional sharp humor, and arrived somewhere that genuinely looks like peace. Her 37.9 million Instagram followers are watching closely, flooding every post with heart emojis and blessings. The industry is watching too. When she returns from maternity leave — and she will, because she said she would, and Samantha doesn't bluff — she'll come back to a landscape she's already reshaped. For now, though, June felt like a fairy tale. And December is going to be something even better.
